units.title: Cycle generators prove phi(2n) divides n factorial
units.statement: There are (n−1)! cycles of length n on n labelled points. Each cyclic subgroup generated by such a cycle has exactly phi(n) generators, so phi(n) divides (n−1)!. If n is odd, phi(2n)=phi(n); if n is even, phi(2n)=2phi(n), and the even factor n supplies the extra two. Thus phi(2n) divides n! for every n≥1.
steps: Partition n-cycles by the cyclic subgroup they generate
Relate phi(2n) to phi(n) by parity
